newsitem.title: INDONESIA: JAKARTA STOCKS END DOWN ON RATE HIKES, RUPIAH FALL.
newsitem.headline: JAKARTA STOCKS END DOWN ON RATE HIKES, RUPIAH FALL.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended down on Wednesday on the back of the central bank's decision to raise interest rates and the rupiah's plunge to a historic low, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index ended down 4.34 points, or 0.66 percent, at 658.60 points. Decliners led advancers by 74 to 41 with 62 issues unchanged.
Total turn-over was estimated at 315 billion rupiah.
"The central bank's move and the rupiah's fresh plunge have provided more reasons for players to reduce exposure in the market," one broker with a large local brokerage firm said.

Indonesia's central bank, Bank Indonesia, raised interest rates for central bank certificates (SBIs) of all maturities by 100 basis points on Wednesday in a move which currency dealers said was aimed at reducing speculative attacks on the rupiah.
The rupiah fell to a new historic low at 2,682 against the dollar at 0630 GMT compared with an opening of 2,643/50 on sustained offshore selling, dealers said.
It recovered slightly to 2,645/55 at 0930 GMT after the central bank intervened in the market.
Brokers said sentiment had already been weak due to reports of possibly higher inflation this year if the ongoing drought in the country was prolonged.

Indonesia's Central Bureau of Statistics (BPS) said the country's inflation rate this year was likely to be higher than the previous forecast of six percent if the drought continues and the negative impacts could not be contained, Bisnis Indonesia newspaper reported.
Brokers said falls were across the board, with commodities-related counters and bank and finance stocks especially hard-hit.
Food company Indofood, tapioca starch producer Budi Acid and snack-food firm Mayora were among the losers as the drought was likely to cut supply of raw materials, brokers said.
Brokers said sentiment was likely to remain weak on Thursday, with the central bank's rate hikes and the weaker rupiah continuing to be the main concerns.
